expectations.text: Output includes a structured JSON schema with store_name, date, items[], total_centavos, payment_method fields
expectations.evidence: Schema includes store_name, receipt_date, line_items[], total_amount, and payment_method. However, there is NO total_centavos field. Amounts are specified in ₱ (pesos), not centavos. The schema uses total_amount (in pesos) rather than total_centavos.

expectations.text: Monetary amounts specified in centavos (not pesos with decimals)
expectations.evidence: All monetary fields use peso amounts: total_amount (₱), unit_price (₱), total_price (₱). No centavos specification. Lines 58-59 show unit_price and total_price described as '(₱)' without centavo conversion. Line 157-158 shows total_amount described as 'Grand total in ₱'.

The schema includes confidence_flags array (lines 191-203) which contains categorical flags ('crumpled_or_faded', 'angled_photo', etc.), NOT per-field numerical confidence scores (0.0-1.0). This is a binary flag array approach, not a scoring approach.

expectations.text: Mentions handling of crumpled receipts, thermal fade, and handwritten amounts
expectations.evidence: Line 11 mentions 'crumpled, faded, angled, low-light, or poorly scanned receipts'. Line 95 includes confidence flag 'crumpled_or_faded'. Lines 112-116 discuss 'Crumpled / Low-Quality Receipts'. Line 122-124 covers 'Handwritten Receipts'. Lines 318 and 318 test thermal receipts. Handwritten amounts covered in line 124.

Lines 12 mention 'payment screenshots (GCash, bank transfers, e-wallet confirmations)'. Lines 19-20 explicitly list 'GCash receipts' and 'Bank/e-wallet receipts' including Maya. Lines 106-110 detail GCash extraction rules. Line 311-312 include QA test cases for GCash screenshots with/without merchant name. Line 313 includes Maya in the test checklist.

expectations.text: Specifies claude-haiku-4-5 as the model (not Sonnet)
expectations.evidence: Line 1 title mentions 'Claude Haiku Vision System Prompt'. Line 241 in the implementation section specifies: 'model: 'claude-haiku-4-5-20250101''. This confirms Haiku, not Sonnet.

expectations.text: Includes warnings array for edge case reporting
expectations.evidence: Lines 191-203 define 'confidence_flags' as an array of enum values that serve as warnings for edge cases: crumpled_or_faded, angled_photo, partial_ocr, illegible_amount, gcash_no_merchant, low_light, requires_manual_verification, handwritten, multiple_pages_partial. Line 202 states: 'Array of confidence warnings. Empty [] if high confidence.'
